key_insight: Charge-aware machine-learning potentials enable near-DFT-accuracy simulations of CrSBr, revealing that sulfur vacancies can lower the chromium Frenkel-pair migration barrier by up to 1.1 eV.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports atomistic studies of defect engineering and beam-induced structural changes in CrSBr for potential magneto-optoelectronic applications.
method: Develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials for Cr–S–Br, including charge-aware qNEP.
Use nudged elastic band calculations to assess vacancy-assisted chromium migration.
Calculate displacement thresholds to compare species susceptibility to electron-beam damage.
evidence_signal: qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy for lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and anisotropic pressure response, while displacement calculations identify Br as the most susceptible species.
watch_item: Transferability to defect configurations and irradiation conditions beyond those benchmarked remains to be established.
paper_title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
